title: 1952 AHSME Problem 21
statement: The sides of a regular polygon of \(n\) sides, \(n\gt4,\) are extended to form a star. The number of degrees at each point of the star is:

solutions.text:
Each exterior angle of a regular \(n\)-gon is \(\frac{360}{n}\) degrees. The two sides forming a point of the star, together with the intervening polygon side, make a triangle whose two base angles are those exterior angles. Hence its point angle is \[ 180-2\left(\frac{360}{n}\right) =\frac{(n-4)180}{n}. \]

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Relate a star point to the exterior angle at each of its two base vertices
The angle at a star point and two exterior angles of the regular polygon form a straight-angle triangle
